messages.author: 42c4bdce94f52d00
messages.subject: Hardware requirements
parts:
Hi everyone,
I am new to natverse and trying to decide what machine to use to make the most out of it. I will mainly use nat, nblast, and possibly some of the other packages (catmaid?). I currently have a relatively new macbook pro but was wondering if something more powerful might be required, especially in terms of GPU for 3D plotting and interactions with rgl?
Many thanks in advance for your help,
Vincent

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Hardware requirements
parts:
Dear Vincent,

A new MacBook Pro will be great for plotting and general analysis. The only thing that may cause a problem is memory if you are trying to do large amounts of NBLAST using the parallel option. When NBLASTing all 25,000 hemibrain neurons vs each other, usage is order 20-30 GB per parallel core. Naturally there are ways to improve the memory efficiency but it's one of those things on the long todo … 

Note that this is only a concern if you plan to do all by all NBLAST. If you are querying a single or a few neurons against a big database of neurons it's not a problem. If you do want to do all by all NBLAST on many neurons, RAM is the main issue – I would go for 256 GB and up i.e. a workstation or server. But I would not do that until you have a demonstrated need.

In fact RAM is the only really limiting resource in my experience. I have a 32GB RAM MBP and there are occasionally times when I am doing very large analyses where I would like to have 64 GB.

In terms of OS, although the natverse is cross platform it is developed on mac/unix and tested on linux; Windows support for some of the more experimental features sometimes lags.

Final point since you mention Macs, we haven't yet tried the natverse on Apple M1 ARM hardware. It is likely to work fine under the rosetta translation, but it may be some months before native ARM versions of R and all the relevant packages are available.

All the best,

Greg.
